title: Body plan viewer: fill a DSL body plan of the subject's anatomy with labelled segments from several scans, one slot at a time, building the final mesh
user-messages: So I want what I think I'm going to be calling a body plan viewer tool. And essentially how it would work is it would take a bunch of segmented models, for example, the crawfish, as well as a body plan written in a DSL. And would lead the user through a series of choices based on the existing labels in the segmentation that's already been done.

> 3. What “final mesh” means here. Parts from different scans have to be joined somehow. I’d show each chosen part in place in its own scan’s coordinates on the left, with no stitching, and leave joining them into one clean mesh to a later ticket. Is that enough for this ticket, or do you want a single exported mesh out of it?

we have csg package as well as mesh boolean nodes that should be using it, then to export we'd run the quad layout pipeline to get the final quad mesh and bake the higher poly normals onto the quad mesh,

> The camera can already build a projection for a smaller view (Camera3D.updateProjection takes an aspect ratio). So my plan is to draw each slot’s segment with the existing mesh renderer, clipped to the slot’s rectangle. That adds no new UI widget, but it is a new way of drawing. OK?

there is a view abstraction that we should use that the the terminal and code pane use for new render targets

> walking_leg_left_2 and walking_leg_right_2 share a picker? Sharing would mean mirroring, and the symmetry work (CRAW-18) isn’t done. I’d keep left and right as separate pickers for now

I'd want the numbers to be interchangeable as well as right/left

> 4. Which scans to test on. On master only IMG_4111 (84 labels) and IMG_4112 (54) carry labels. IMG_4109/4110 have rings but no labels, and IMG_4113–4118 are being labelled in the six segmentation worktrees (CRAW-95…100, 24–43 labels each). I’d copy three or four of those labelled files into tmp/ to test with, rather than wait for them to land.

5. yes, also need to be a tree

> 4. Which scans to test on. On master only IMG_4111 (84 labels) and IMG_4112 (54) carry labels. IMG_4109/4110 have rings but no labels, and IMG_4113–4118 are being labelled in the six segmentation worktrees (CRAW-95…100, 24–43 labels each). I’d copy three or four of those labelled files into tmp/ to test with, rather than wait for them to land.

6. tool on the ring scene

this happened about halfway thoruhg me picking parts, not sure why or what you are adding to memory in the meantime, is it even possible to pick all of the parts? are you doing csg in intermediate steps or at the end?

need to think about how we can keep the parts finished mesh as the only things in memory, also the parts are just hollow pieces when we should be using solids so they can fit each other, there is also something weird going on on the canvas where when Iscroll halfway over a part's box the part disapears when it overlaps with the scroll bar, also it is a little wierd that the part rotates only when the main view rotates and you cannot rotate in the body plan view, also there is something weird where the various parts are not rotateing from the same origin in the main view, so rotating the bigger pieces makes sense but then the small pieces change their position relative to teh big pieces. Also I think there is  something missing in that the segmentation of each piece should tell use how it is intended to connect to the next piece in the chain (since the hole that is left by the next piece  being segmented is where we should fill in with the next part regardless of what mesh it originated from. for example on the crawfish there are two pieces to the claw one that is bigger and one that is opposable and smaller, and the smaller piece is segmented from the bigger piece leaving a hole that should tell you where to attach the smaller piece regardless if the smaller peice comes from mesh 1 or 999. Also a body plan should allow for symmetry as well as breaking symmetry, so for parts that are symetrical I should only really have to choose once and the choice should be reflected across both axises of the body plan, but We'll have to think about how to break that symmetry.
description:
User request 2026-11-07. A body plan viewer: a tool that takes a set of segmented, part-labelled models (for example the crawfish scans IMG_4109-4118, labelled with add_label statements such as "telson", "tail_segment_4_dorsal", "uropod_left_outer") plus a body plan written in a DSL, and walks the user through one choice per body plan slot, picking each slot's part from the labelled segments. The output is one final mesh built from the anatomy of the underlying model or real-world object.

Body plan. A DSL description of the subject's anatomy: which parts it has and how they chain and attach (a finger is three segments, each attached to the one before; a crawfish has N walking legs, M abdominal segments, antennae that attach to the head in a given way, and so on). It is written in Ixdar's one language (.dsl), not a sibling format. A skill authors it for a new subject: look the anatomy up (Wikipedia or similar) or work from the model's own knowledge, and cross-check against the labels the segmentation already has. The segmentation already carries part of this structure; the body plan is the template the chosen segments fill in.

Screen layout.
- Right side, at least half the screen (full screen is not required): a 2D graph of the body plan, drawn like the DSL graph view (DslGraphView / DslGraphLayout: boxes, bezier connections, its own Camera2D and CanvasScroll), but showing body plan slots instead of DSL nodes.
- On each body plan slot: a small 3D mesh view of the segment currently offered for that slot.
- Under that view, a horizontal bar with an arrow at each end to step through the candidate segments, showing the label the segment has in its source mesh. Every segment with the same label (across all the loaded models) sits in the same picker.
- A check-mark button that confirms the current slot's choice and moves to the next slot in the sequence (a finger's three segments in chain order, for example).
- Left side: the assembled model, updated live as choices are made.
- When every slot is chosen, the user is told they are done; the user suggested the existing error toast (ErrorToasts) as the way to say it.

User ruling: use the existing infrastructure for all of this and do not invent new UI elements. The arrows are MenuScrollBar's end arrows (clickable, already drawn with SDFLine), the check mark is a MenuButton, the graph is DslGraphView's drawing and layout, the done message is ErrorToasts. Anything that genuinely does not exist yet (see unknowns) is raised with the user before it is built.

Relation to CRAW-65 (part chooser: compare each named part across the scans of a collection and pick the best copy of each): same idea of picking per-part from several segmented scans; this ticket adds the body plan as the structure that drives the sequence and the assembled result. Decide with the user whether this supersedes CRAW-65 or builds on it.

User ruling 2026-11-07: CRAW-65 is archived in favour of this ticket. Carry over from it: an ixdar-cli route that lists body plan slots, the candidate segments per slot (which scan, which label) and the current choice, so agents can read it; and showing, per scan, which slots it has no segment for.

User rulings 2026-11-07, before implementation:
- Small 3D views: use the view abstraction the terminal and code pane use for their own render targets; no ad-hoc viewport clipping.
- Pickers: left/right are interchangeable and so are the instance numbers (walking_leg_left_1 and walking_leg_right_3 can fill the same slot). A candidate taken from the other side is mirrored with the existing mirror node (MirrorGeometryNode). The slot's label pattern decides which names match.
- Final mesh: join the chosen parts with the mesh boolean nodes (MeshBooleanNode over the geometry/mesh/csg package), then run the quad layout pipeline to get the final quad mesh. Baking the high-poly normals onto that quad mesh is a separate ticket, not this one.
- Test scans: copy three or four labelled scans (IMG_4111, IMG_4112 from master; IMG_4113-4118 from the segmentation worktrees) into tmp/.
- Body plan DSL: one body_part statement per slot (parent slot, labels that fill it), the choices saved as parameters on the same statements; the body plan is a tree (each slot has at most one parent).
- Placement: a tool on the ring scene (RingScene), not a new scene.
definition-of-done:
1. A body plan DSL exists, is documented, and a crawfish body plan (legs, abdominal segments, head, antennae, claws, telson, uropods, with their chaining) is written in it under src/main/resources/dsl/ and loads without error.
2. A skill (under ai-workspace/.claude/skills/) tells an agent how to research a subject's anatomy and write its body plan in that DSL, checked against the labels the subject's segmentations already carry.
3. A scene/tool loads a set of labelled models plus a body plan and shows the body plan as a 2D graph covering at least half the screen, drawn with the DslGraphView/DslGraphLayout machinery.
4. Each slot shows a small 3D view of its current candidate, a bar under it with MenuScrollBar arrows that step through candidates and show each candidate's source label, all same-labelled segments from every model in one picker, and a MenuButton check mark that confirms and moves to the next slot in chain order.
5. The left side shows the assembled model and updates on every confirmation.
6. After the last slot the user is told they are done (ErrorToasts unless the user rules otherwise).
7. No new UI widget classes: every control is an existing class; anything missing was raised with the user first and their ruling is recorded on the ticket.
8. The choices persist as DSL (part chosen per slot identified by model and surface point, never by face or vertex id) and reload.
9. Verified on at least three labelled crawfish scans; launch entry and screenshots under tmp/.

10. An ixdar-cli route lists slots, candidates per slot (scan and label) and current choices; slots a scan has no segment for are shown as missing.
testing-plan:
1. Load three labelled crawfish scans with the crawfish body plan; step through every slot with the arrows and check mark; screenshot the graph, a slot's picker and the assembled model mid-way and at the end.
2. Confirm same-labelled segments from different scans appear in one picker and that the bar shows each one's source label.
3. Save, reload the scene, and confirm the choices and assembled model come back.
4. Write a small body plan by hand (a three-segment finger on the hand DSL models) to check chaining order outside the crawfish.
unknowns: Whether the done message should really use the error toast or something already existing that reads as success.

First load of a plan whose scans have no cached parts still takes about 25 s, about 23 s of it the scans' own segmentation graphs (repair_mesh about half); under 10 s needs faster segmentation or the scans run side by side on a larger heap.

IMG_4112 (tail_segment_5_side_right, tail_segment_4_underside_right, tail_segment_3_dorsal, tail_joint_rear, claw_right_merus_lower) and IMG_4113 (antenna_base) have labels that resolve to no region, so candidates using them have gaps; fix in those scans' segmentations?
changes-made:
New nodes body_plan (loads segmented scans, resolves their labels, outputs the plan in the _body_plan slot) and body_part (one slot: parent, label pattern, choice; outputs the chosen part cut closed, mirrored when it comes from the other side). Label patterns (BodyPartCandidates): # interchangeable numbers, * pieces of one part, left/right interchangeable with mirroring, ; alternatives. Choices persist as "<scan> @ x,y,z" (a surface point, never a face or vertex id).
crawfish/body_plan.dsl: 55 slots as a tree (carapace, head shield, rostrum, eyes, antennules, antennae, thorax underside, both claws base to fingers, 4x2 walking legs of 3 segments, tail joint, 6 tail segments, telson, uropods).
BodyPlanTool (ring scene, ctrl+B): left half the assembled body (filled slots, current one highlighted); right half the plan's DslGraphView in its own scene view, each body_part box holding the candidate's 3D view, its source label, a MenuScrollBar picker and a MenuButton OK. Enter/OK confirms, writes the choice to the .dsl and moves to the next unfilled slot; Left/Right step candidates, Up/Down change slot, a click on a box selects it. The last confirm writes a chain of mesh_boolean UNIONs plus quad_layout (body_quads) and says done in the ErrorToasts toast. An unfilled slot opens on the first candidate no other slot of its pattern holds.
Infrastructure reused, small extensions: Camera3D.viewBounds (aspect of a sub-view), DslGraphLayout.reservedWidth/Height (room in a box), DslGraphView(scene, view) + reserve hook, MeshAppend reverses winding under a reflection, MirrorGeometryNode.reflection, SeparateGeometryNode.extractFaces public.
Route ixdar-cli body-plan: slots, candidates per slot (scan, labels, mirrored), choices, missing_in scans.
Skill ai-workspace/.claude/skills/body-plan/SKILL.md: research anatomy, read scan labels, write and check the plan.
Unit test unit.mesh.BodyPartCandidatesTest (4 tests).
Verified on 4 labelled scans (IMG_4111, IMG_4112 from master; IMG_4113 from craw-95, IMG_4115 from craw-97, copied to tmp/craw-103/): walked all 55 slots, mouse arrows and OK, reload restores all 55 choices and the assembled body; re-confirming after done rewrites the union block identically.

Second round, after the user's out-of-memory report and feedback.
Memory: BodyPartLibrary cuts each scan once (RingRegionExtraction.cut(), then keep() per label, falling back to face regions for labels the component vote left without pieces) into compact ArrayMesh solids plus per-label joints (midpoints of the boundary shared with each neighbouring label), caches them under the app cache (body-plan/<scan>-<hash of the .dsl>/, glb parts plus library.json) and drops the scan. First load ~166 s, cached load ~2 s; live heap with all 55 slots filled ~500 MB, against the old out-of-memory at 3.4 GB halfway through.
Solids: every part is the closed cut piece, previews and body alike.
Joints: BodyPlan.place seats a child by its scan's own boundaries: the child's cap (its boundary toward the parent's part, nearest the root) is set into the parent's hole (the parent's boundary toward the child's part, chosen by the slot id's side and numbers) with a similarity transform and the twist that best matches the parent's rotation. A child from the parent's own scan, reflected alike, keeps the scan's own placement beside its parent; one from the parent's scan with no shared boundary stays in place; one from another scan with no hole is drawn in the warning colour and listed as not attached.
Canvas: slot views are scissor-clipped (new GL.scissor / SCISSOR_TEST) to the graph view inside its scroll bars instead of hidden; a drag in a slot's view orbits that slot's own Camera3D; the body view renders every part with its placement transform about one origin.
Symmetry: body_part mirror_of=<left slot>.geometry on the 21 right-side slots; an empty choice follows the partner's twin reflected; a choice of its own breaks the symmetry, Backspace (clear-choice) clears a slot and restores following. Midline parts split into halves already take one choice for both.
Picking: an unfilled slot opens on a free candidate its scan cut from the parent's chosen part (same scan, same side), so chains open in order.
Route body-plan adds per slot follows_partner, joint and attached, and an attached count. Skill body-plan documents mirror_of and choosing parents by the segmentation's boundaries. Unit test oneLabelMatchesOnEitherSideWithAnyNumber (5 tests).
Verified headless on the 4 scans: Enter walk fills all 55 slots (21 following their partners), 50 attached; the 5 unattached are the rostrum (IMG_4113's rostrum shares no boundary with any labelled part) and four leg tips the walk took from other scans. Assembled body reads as one crayfish (tmp/craw-103-v4-top.png, tmp/craw-103-v4-side.png); Backspace clear, twin breaking and restoring, slot-view orbit (tmp/craw-103-v4-after-drag.png) checked.

First-load time: a cold load (no part cache) took 163 s. Profiled with JFR, about 140 s of it was capping each label's piece with the full MeshRepair (ray-cast exposed-face pruning and the Liepa fill faired by conjugate gradient), one label at a time on the main thread. Now RingRegionExtraction.quickCaps (through a new MeshRepair.fairFills switch) caps body-plan pieces with the refined, unfaired fill and no pruning, since they are pieces of a surface repair_mesh already cleaned; and the labels cap in parallel, each on RingRegionExtraction.sharingCut(), a copy that shares the cut read-only. Same parts and the same closure as before (all closed except IMG_4115 labels 28 and 30, open both ways). Cold load 163 s -> 25.5 s; cached load 1.9 s. The remaining ~23 s is the four scans' own segmentation graphs (IMG_4111 6.3 s, IMG_4112 5.6 s, IMG_4113 6.2 s, IMG_4115 4.9 s, repair_mesh about half of each), the same cost as opening each scan in the ring scene. Running the scans side by side ran out of the default ~4 GB heap inside repair_mesh, so they stay one at a time.

Caps and depth, after the user's screenshots of a hollow tail ring and a part showing through another. The quick-cap switch (unfaired fill, no pruning) is removed: parts are capped exactly as the region tool caps a selection. Parts are now capped per candidate, not per label: the library keeps each label's open piece of the cut, and BodyPartLibrary.closedLater welds a candidate's pieces along the boundaries they share and runs MeshRepair once, so each opening left (a tail segment's front and back) is filled on its own; closed parts are cached as closed_<labels>.glb and the tool starts capping every slot's candidates in the background when the plan loads (BodyPlan.prepare). Labels no longer overlap: a piece a leaking cut ran into several labels' regions (IMG_4111's tail_segment_2_dorsal had swallowed side_left and underside_left) is split by its faces' regions (RingRegionExtraction.leakedPieceShare, set to MIXED_COMPONENT_SHARE; zero, the region tool's default, never does). Depth: every part in the body view now shares one far plane (HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.projectionExtent, set from the placed parts' extent round the orbit target); each runtime had fitted its far plane to its own size, so small parts' depths did not compare with the body's. Cold load 34 s (scan graphs about 23 s of it), cached 2 s. Labels that resolve to no region and so leave gaps in their candidates: IMG_4112 tail_segment_5_side_right, tail_segment_4_underside_right, tail_segment_3_dorsal, tail_joint_rear, claw_right_merus_lower; IMG_4113 antenna_base.

No capping in the background for minutes. The tool no longer starts capping every slot's candidates when the plan loads. It caps only the current slot's pick and its two neighbours (BodyPlan.prepare from place). While a part's cap is still running, the tool shows its open labelled pieces (BodyPlan.shownPart / openPart), so stepping through candidates never waits: the tool opens in about 0.6 s and each step takes about 0.3 s uncached. body_plan now starts capping every chosen slot's part at once when the graph loads (BodyPartNode.literal read off the declared body_part statements), so the body_part statements find their parts ready instead of capping them one after another. Fully chosen plan (34 choices): cold load down from 51 s to 27 s (scan graphs 18 s, parts 9 s); cached load 1.7 s.

No file caching. At the user's request, the body plan no longer writes or reads anything on disk. BodyPartLibrary.of, the manifest and the label_/closed_ .glb files are gone; body_plan runs each scan's graph every load and calls BodyPartLibrary.cut. Capped parts are kept only in memory, for the session. This supersedes the earlier notes about ~/.cache/ixdar/body-plan, the cached 1.7 s load and closed_<labels>.glb. Fully chosen plan (34 choices): every load now takes about 30 s (scan graphs 18 s, the 34 parts capped in parallel 11.5 s).

Hole-fill fairing by sparse Cholesky. A JFR profile of a fully chosen plan's load showed that capping the parts spent 83% of its time in MeshHoleFiller.fair: a matrix-free conjugate gradient with no preconditioner, aiming for a 1e-12 tolerance on the umbrella normal equations. On the large openings a cut leaves (600-1600 boundary edges, 15-30k unknowns) it ran out its 4000 iterations unconverged: 35 of 3021 solves took 74 s of the 92 s of summed solve CPU. fair() now assembles U^T U (U = D^-1 A - I over the patch and its held ring) as a NormalMatrix, factors it once with DirectSolver (AMD ordering, PARDISO on desktop, EJML otherwise) and solves x, y and z. The held vertices' columns are folded into the right-hand side. The result is the exact minimiser the CG was approaching. The unused fairingIterations field and the CG constants are gone. This affects every MeshHoleFiller user (repair_mesh, region tool caps, body plan caps). The scans' repair_mesh reports are identical, and MeshRepairTest passes (15/15). Fully chosen plan load: 27.9 s -> 20.8 s; body_part (capping 34 parts) 9.5 s -> 3.1 s. The scans' graphs and the library cut are still about 17.7 s.

Faster library cut. RingRegionExtraction.cut: a ring with no spline walls its marked edges from RingRegions.ringEdgeIds instead of scanning every mesh edge once per ring; each face's boundary is read straight from its half-edges with no per-edge arrays; a face no ring crosses becomes its one triangle without the piece lists; and the cut triangles are paired through the source mesh's half-edges (each edge segment between inserted vertices holds the corner waiting for the triangle across it, and a split face's own triangles pair among themselves) instead of a boxed HashMap over every triangle edge. neighbourByCorner is now public, and BodyPartLibrary.cut reads its joints from it instead of pairing every edge again. Output is identical on IMG_4111, 4112, 4113 and 4115: cut triangles, parents, adjacency, pieces, piece regions, walls, problems, and the library's parts, centroids and joints (fingerprints compared before and after). Warm, per scan: extraction.cut 650-860 ms -> 130-270 ms; whole BodyPartLibrary.cut for four scans 3.2 s -> 1.3 s. In the app's profile the library cut's main-thread samples fell from 438 to about 130. RingRegionExtractionTest, RingRegionsTest, RingRegionsUpdateTest, MeshRepairTest, BodyPartCandidatesTest, BisectorTest and ConformingLoopSnapTest pass (47 tests). The region tool shares the faster cut.

Attach mode and the "none" choice in the body plan tool.
- body_part choice="none": the slot holds no part. Its children seat on the part above it. A part from the same scan sits where its own cap met that part. A part from another scan takes the empty slot's hole. Past an empty slot a part keeps its own size. Mirrored partners follow "none" as well.
- body_part attach="x,y,z": a point on the parent's part where the slot's part seats instead of its hole. The part slides there and tilts to the surface; its twist and size stay the same.
- Body plan tool: the picker has a "none" entry after the last candidate. J toggles attach mode: the current part is drawn see-through, with a dot where it joins the part above. Dragging the dot along that part moves it, and on release attach is written for the slot and, reflected, for its mirror partner. Backspace in attach mode puts the part back in its hole.
- HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.renderSeeThrough is shared with MeshNodeViewerScene. It leaves blending on, as the scene set it. Turning blending off broke every later text and line draw.
- RingDslWriter.statementLine and insertAfter are restored; TOOL-57 removed them as unused.
Verified: headless plan reports for the none, attach and full plans. In the app: attach mode, a drag of the dot (both statements written) and the none entry, screenshots tmp/craw-103/attach_mode.png, attach_mode_head.png, none_picker.png. Tests: RingRegionExtraction, RingRegions, RingRegionsUpdate, MeshRepair, BodyPartCandidates, Bisector, ConformingLoopSnap, 47 passing.
review-summary: The body plan tool now builds each scan's parts once as cached solids and seats every child part in the hole its scan cut it from, with right-side slots mirroring their left partner. Picking all 55 slots ran out of memory, and parts floated loose with no shared origin.
